scores.evidence:
SPLIT THE SLASH. The requirement is a compound OR. The two halves score very differently and must not be averaged into a single vague number.

=== HALF A — DATA ENGINEERING: MET, and met deeply. 9/10 ===

Recent (Mar 2025 – Apr 2026, Amura/VoltusWave), from `killer-query-case-studies/kq4-early-signal-detection.html`. This is elite-tier data engineering, not adjacent:
- "The platform's source of truth is an append-only event spine (DynamoDB). A projection keeps a decision graph (Neptune) current, and a deterministic nightly export freezes it to columnar snapshot files."
- "Parquet + DuckDB — Snapshot-only store: frozen vertices and edges plus the ungated observation snapshot; sequence, score, and dependency tables partitioned by tenant and snapshot hash."
- Nine-year hydration as a first-class pipeline: "Roughly nine years of prior history — check-ins, labs, decisions, and the relapse outcomes themselves — were hydrated through the same append-only event spine that carries live traffic"; "Content-addressed event IDs and conditional writes make the load idempotent and resumable: re-running the pipeline over the same corpus yields a byte-identical spine and an identical snapshot-manifest hash."
- Event-time provenance with a load-failing assertion: "A hard invariant — every historical event's real-world time must fall strictly before its received time — turns the cardinal sin into a caught error rather than a silent one."
- Fenced cutover with a boundary proof: "first_live_seq is fence_seq + 1 · no hole"; "a single missing sequence number aborts the cutover."
- Schema evolution and quarantine: "Nine years spans many legacy payload-schema versions; each gets an explicit upconverter, and any row that cannot be mapped to a schema — or to a tenant — is quarantined with a reason rather than defaulted."
- Structured AND unstructured, which the JD asks for by name: clinical events into sequences (KQ4) plus free-text into embeddings — `kq1-precedent-search.html`: "Embed self-hosted model in-VPC cached by content_hash + model_version" → "Elasticsearch dense_vector authoritative serving index".

The years behind it, from `professional-journey.md` — this is what makes 5+ defensible on the data half:
- 2012, McDonald's (l.166, his own narration): "field-level lineage so leadership could see when each value was first seen and last changed. That was 2012, before anyone called it data provenance."
- 2016–17, Teletext (l.84): "Elasticsearch cache with TTL and in-house replacement of a third-party pricing service (Teletext), cross-supplier entity reconciliation (Teletext)" — plus the GIATA reconciliation pipeline "automate[d] … on AWS Lambda, keeping the approval step yourself" (l.446). Master résumé: "Cut operational cost **46%** by retiring a third-party pricing product for an in-house **ELK** cache".
- 2019–25, Deque (l.80): "PostgreSQL 9.6 → Aurora PostgreSQL 13.x with zero downtime" across ~300 instances — data-platform work, honestly weighted lower than pipeline engineering.
- 2025–26 (l.80): "DynamoDB + OpenSearch (Voltuswave 2nd stint)".
Cumulative data-engineering exposure runs 2012 → 2026; the concentrated, unambiguous stretches are Teletext (~1 yr), Deque platform/DB (partial across 5 yrs) and Amura (~1 yr). "5+ years" survives an honest audit on this half.

=== HALF B — DEEP LEARNING: SHORT. Not "nearly met". 5/10 ===

Applied production DL is ONE YEAR, and the record says so in one line. `professional-journey.md` l.86–88, the entire "AI / ML in production" section:
  "## AI / ML in production
   Voltuswave 2nd stint — Killer Query programme, event spine projected via Lambda into Amazon Neptune, dense vectors, RAG pipeline, piloted to doctors and sales."
One stint. Mar 2025 – Apr 2026 = ~14 months. The five years immediately before it (Deque, Dec 2019 – Feb 2025) contain no ML content anywhere in the journey doc — that section is multi-tenancy, Spring Boot, Keycloak→Red Hat SSO, Aurora.

The diploma adds credibility, not years — `professional-journey.md` l.40: "PG Diploma in AI/ML, IIIT Bangalore (Jan 2021)." It sits in the file as a single line with no accompanying project, employer or artefact. It cannot be counted as applied years and must not be stretched into any.

What the one year actually contains — genuinely senior, genuinely narrow (`kq4`):
- A real trained sequence model with a promotion ladder: "Rung 1 · Logistic baseline · sets the floor" → "Rung 2 · does PrefixSpan beat logistic on calibrated precision-recall" → "Rung 3 · does the Transformer beat PrefixSpan AND keep attribution faithful".
- Deployment: "SageMaker — Hosts the sequence model and runs nightly batch-transform scoring"; "SageMaker InvokeEndpoint tenant header asserted".
- The leakage/label discipline that is the hard part: "the centre of this system is not the transformer; it is the time geometry that decides what is a positive, what is a negative, and what is not yet allowed to be either"; enforced enum "mature, not_mature, censored_dropout, program_switch, by_later_relapse"; "Time-cut back-tests only — never a random split."
Master résumé carries it as: "Sequenced patient event histories into a relapse early-warning model on **Amazon SageMaker**, gated never to train on an outcome window that had not matured".

But note what the DL work deliberately is NOT, in his own documents — this is where a probing interviewer lands:
- KQ1: "ranking is vector math, not a model" — retrieval quality comes from a PRE-TRAINED, self-hosted embedder, not a model he trained or fine-tuned.
- KQ4 §07: "nothing in the scoring or alerting path routes through an LLM at all"; "There is no persona, no prompt, and no generated sentence anywhere in the alerting path."
The portfolio's stated through-line is "knowing when not to use an LLM." That is an architecture virtue and it reads as one — but it means the deep-learning surface area under his hands is one transformer rung plus inference-serving of pre-trained models. There is no fine-tuning, no pre-training, no CV, no RL anywhere in the corpus.

=== MLOps, which the JD names separately and which partly rescues the DL half — strong, 8/10 ===
- Retraining pipelines, named: "SageMaker Pipelines — Weekly retrain with the three-way promotion gate and leakage assertions; a promotion swaps the endpoint and invalidates the entire risk cache namespace."
- Drift detection, named twice: "Tokenizer drift — vocab + frequency — Drift on the token vocabulary or its distribution triggers a retrain before scores quietly decay under a shifting event stream"; "Calibration — Brier + reliability slices — Per-tenant and per-program reliability, with drift-triggered recalibration."
- Model versioning and safe swap: canonical cache key "pins the tokenizer, the model version, the snapshot hash, and the patient's latest event sequence"; "it invalidates the entire risk-cache namespace BEFORE it repoints the serving endpoint at the new model version… reverse it, and a coach could read a fresh cache entry scored by a model that no longer exists."
- Champion/challenger: "Does the candidate beat the live champion at the operating point" → "Promote · swap endpoint · flush the risk cache".
Of the JD's three named MLOps artefacts — "model registries, retraining pipelines, drift detection" — retraining and drift are directly evidenced; a model REGISTRY is never named, only implied by model_version pins plus champion/challenger promotion.

=== The metric floor, which constrains every claim above ===
`kq4` footer: "every figure on this page is a pre-registered acceptance target, and the observed results are not mine to publish." So ≥0.40 precision, ≥3× lift, ≥80% coverage are TARGETS. Nothing in the DL half can be presented as an achieved result.
gaps: DEEP-LEARNING DURATION — CAPABILITY CAP (the binding one). ~14 months applied (Mar 2025 – Apr 2026) plus a Jan 2021 diploma, against a 5+ year bar. Duration cannot be ramped, taught, or re-vectored — it is the one gap on this JD with no honest lift. It caps this criterion and nothing else will move it.

DEQUE'S FIVE YEARS ARE NOT DL YEARS — CAPABILITY CAP (structural). Dec 2019 – Feb 2025 is the largest recent block on the résumé and the journey doc's ML section does not mention it once. Any reader doing the arithmetic gets 'one year of AI' from a 19-year résumé. This is what makes the shortfall visible at screen, before anyone reads KQ4.

NO MODEL TRAINING BEYOND ONE SEQUENCE MODEL — CAPABILITY CAP (narrow, partial). No fine-tuning, no pre-training, no computer vision, no reinforcement learning anywhere in the corpus. KQ1 states it outright: 'ranking is vector math, not a model'. The embedder is pre-trained and self-hosted, i.e. DL deployment rather than DL development.

WHICH RUNG IS ACTUALLY LIVE — EVIDENCE GAP / prep item, not a scoring item. The ladder ships 'the simplest model that cleared its bar'; nothing in KQ4 says the Transformer won. 'So is a transformer in production, or is it logistic regression?' is a near-certain question and there is no documented answer. He must be able to say honestly which rung the promotion gate selected, or that he left before it settled.

MODEL REGISTRY NOT NAMED — RAMP ITEM (small). The JD names 'model registries'; the corpus evidences the function (model_version pins, champion/challenger promotion, endpoint swap, SageMaker Pipelines) but never the artefact. SageMaker Model Registry is a days-long ramp on a stack he already runs.

APACHE SPARK / BIG-DATA FRAMEWORKS — RAMP ITEM (real, not trivial). DuckDB + Parquet + Kinesis demonstrate columnar analytics, snapshot determinism and stream partitioning, but Spark is absent and is what 'big data frameworks' usually means at an enterprise product company. Adjacent, not equivalent — do not let this get scored as present.

DIFFUSION MODELS AND STATE-SPACE MODELS — RAMP ITEM (do not claim, at all). Present only in the Naukri tag list, absent from the JD body's core requirements and absent from every one of his documents. Scoring these as present would be the cardinal sin; claiming them in a room would be worse.

NO MEASURED DL OUTCOMES — CONSTRAINT on how the year can be presented. Precision ≥0.40, lift ≥3×, coverage ≥80% are pre-registered acceptance targets. He can describe design, scale and discipline; he cannot say the model performed. Every DL bullet must stay design-and-scale shaped.
SCALA / KOTLIN / RUST — RAMP ITEM (explicitly 'desirable', not required). Absent. Should not touch this score and should not be mentioned outward.
scores.ramp_vs_cap: CAP on the deep-learning half — and it is a duration cap, the only kind that cannot be closed by re-vectoring real work. ~14 months applied against 5+ years asked. No Rule 7 edit, no new bullet and no honest re-reading fixes four missing years; the smallest honest lift here is presentational, not evidential. NOT A CAP on the compound requirement as written: "5+ years in deep learning / data engineering" is a slash, and the data-engineering half clears it on its own with a decade of exposure and an unusually deep final year. Everything else on this criterion is a RAMP ITEM — Spark, a named model registry, diffusion/state-space models, Scala/Kotlin/Rust — and none of them is a genuinely CORE absent technology, so none of them should pull the score further down.
scores.verdict:
7.0/10. Say the plain thing first: THE DEEP-LEARNING HALF IS SHORT — not nearly met, short. About one year of applied production deep learning plus a 2021 diploma, against a five-year bar. Anyone who asks "how many years of deep learning?" gets an answer with a 4-year hole in it, and this is the single most likely place this application dies. Do not soften that anywhere internal.

It scores 7 rather than 5 for three defensible reasons. First, the requirement is written with a slash, and the scoring rules say to read that generously: the DATA-ENGINEERING half satisfies "5+ years" on its own, with real depth — 2012 field-level lineage at McDonald's, the 2016 ELK/entity-reconciliation work at Teletext, the Deque data platform, and then a final year of append-only event spine, deterministic Parquet exporter, DuckDB, four-field event-time provenance and a proof-carrying nine-year hydration that is stronger than most people's whole data-engineering résumé. Second, the JD's own framing is "operates at the INTERSECTION of deep learning, data engineering, software engineering and MLOps" — and the intersection is exactly where he sits. Third, the MLOps evidence is unusually concrete and directly answers the JD's named bullet: weekly retrain through SageMaker Pipelines, tokenizer-drift and calibration-drift monitors, model_version pinned into the cache key, and a promotion that invalidates the namespace before repointing the endpoint. Two of the three named MLOps artefacts are evidenced outright.

It does NOT score 8+ because the seat's centre of gravity is deep learning — it leads the Naukri tags, it leads the role summary, and "deep learning deployment" is a stated focus — and behind that word he has one transformer rung on a promotion ladder plus inference-serving of pre-trained embedders. His own documents say "ranking is vector math, not a model" and "nothing in the scoring or alerting path routes through an LLM at all". That is excellent architecture and honest engineering; it is not five years of deep learning, and an 8 would hide precisely the thing he should be preparing for.

WHAT HE SHOULD ACTUALLY PREPARE, since that is the point of scoring this honestly: (1) a 20-second answer to "five years of DL?" that leads with the data-engineering decade and the intersection, names the one year plainly, and does not apologise — the depth of one year of leakage geometry, label maturity and promotion gating beats three years of notebook work, and he can say why; (2) which rung of the ladder is live, or that he left before the gate settled — there is no documented answer and the question is close to certain; (3) the target-versus-measurement line, said once and cleanly, before an interviewer finds it. Outward-facing material leads with the data-engineering depth and the MLOps discipline and never volunteers the year count.
